candidate_B_full_zero.definition: Nontrivial zero of zeta(s) in the critical strip 0 < beta_n < 1
candidate_B_full_zero.note: Unconditionally, rho_n in Q_bar <=> (beta_n in Q_bar and gamma_n in Q_bar). Conditionally under RH (beta_n = 1/2), rho_n in Q_bar <=> gamma_n in Q_bar.

candidate_C_shifted_ordinate.definition: Real translation of the ordinate gamma_n by the rational constant 1/2

shifted_ordinate_audit.rational_equivalence: gamma in Q  <=>  gamma + 1/2 in Q
shifted_ordinate_audit.algebraic_equivalence: gamma in Q_bar  <=>  gamma + 1/2 in Q_bar
shifted_ordinate_audit.confusion_firewall: gamma + 1/2 in R is a real affine shift of Im(rho), whereas 1/2 + i*gamma in C is the complex zero on the critical line.

rho_vs_gamma_algebraicity.unconditional_equivalence: rho = beta + i*gamma in Q_bar  <=>  (beta in Q_bar and gamma in Q_bar)

unconditional_forward.statement: rho = beta + i*gamma in Q_bar  ==>  beta in Q_bar and gamma in Q_bar
unconditional_forward.proof: Q_bar is a subfield of C stable under complex conjugation (since the minimal polynomial of rho over Q has real rational coefficients, so conj(rho) is also a root). Because i in Q_bar (i^2 + 1 = 0) and 2 in Q_bar, beta = (rho + conj(rho))/2 in Q_bar and gamma = (rho - conj(rho))/(2i) in Q_bar.

unconditional_converse.statement: beta in Q_bar and gamma in Q_bar  ==>  rho = beta + i*gamma in Q_bar
unconditional_converse.proof: Q_bar is a field containing beta, gamma, and i; hence beta + i*gamma in Q_bar.

unconditional_contrapositive.statement: (beta transcendental or gamma transcendental)  ==>  rho = beta + i*gamma transcendental

audit.unconditional_one_way_warning: Unconditionally (without assuming beta in Q_bar), gamma in Q_bar does NOT imply rho in Q_bar unless beta in Q_bar is also known; and rho transcendental does NOT determine which of beta or gamma is transcendental unless beta = 1/2 (or beta in Q_bar) is known.

conditional_rh_equivalence.statement: Under beta = 1/2, rho in Q_bar  <=>  gamma in Q_bar (and rho transcendental <=> gamma transcendental)

if_rho_algebraic: conj(rho) is algebraic of the same degree over Q
quartet polynomial (X^2 - z^2)(X^2 - conj(z)^2) has algebraic coefficients in Q_bar[X]
if_gamma_algebraic_unconditional: Does NOT imply rho = beta + i*gamma in Q_bar unless beta in Q_bar
if_rh_and_gamma_algebraic: rho = 1/2 + i*gamma in Q(gamma, i) subset Q_bar
if_rho_rational: IMPOSSIBLE for nontrivial zeros: gamma_n != 0 because zeta(s) < 0 for all real s in (0, 1) ((1 - 2^{1-s}) zeta(s) = sum_{n>=1} (-1)^{n-1} n^{-s} > 0 while 1 - 2^{1-s} < 0).
if_gamma_rational: Under RH (beta = 1/2), rho = 1/2 + i*gamma lies in the Gaussian rationals Q(i) (imaginary quadratic field of degree 2).

Unconditionally for the first zero gamma_1, excluded for all denominators 1 <= q <= 10000 by 128-bit Arb interval arithmetic, but universal irrationality gamma_n notin Q for all n remains OPEN_IN_LITERATURE.

conditional_rh_equivalences.statement: Under beta = 1/2, rho in Q_bar  <=>  gamma in Q_bar (and rho transcendental <=> gamma transcendental)

rho_n_non_real_for_nontrivial_zeros.statement: Every zero rho in 0 < Re(rho) < 1 satisfies Im(rho) != 0, hence rho notin R and rho notin Q.

gamma_n_irrational.statement: For a specific nontrivial zero ordinate gamma_n (e.g., gamma_1), gamma_n notin Q.
gamma_n_irrational.distinction_note: Explicitly recognized as an open Diophantine problem in the analytic number theory literature (related to the Linear Independence Conjecture of Wintner 1935 / Ingham 1942 / Rubinstein-Sarnak 1994): not even the irrationality of gamma_1 is proved.

gamma_n_transcendental.statement: For a specific nontrivial zero ordinate gamma_n, gamma_n notin Q_bar.
gamma_n_transcendental.distinction_note: Known to be open in the literature; implied by the Grand Linear Independence Conjecture (LI: the positive ordinates gamma_n are Q-linearly independent, or Q_bar-linearly independent), which remains completely unproved.

rho_n_transcendental.statement: For a specific nontrivial zero rho_n = beta_n + i*gamma_n, rho_n notin Q_bar.
rho_n_transcendental.distinction_note: Known to be open; equivalent to transcendence of beta_n or gamma_n.

rho_n_excluded_from_named_number_field.statement: No nontrivial zero rho_n lies in a fixed algebraic number field K (e.g., Q(i)).
rho_n_excluded_from_named_number_field.distinction_note: While finite bounded-height searches exclude small algebraic numbers for a fixed zero gamma_1, no unconditional theorem in the primary literature proves zeta(alpha) != 0 for all alpha in Q(i) cap {0 < Re(s) < 1}.

gamma_n_linear_or_algebraic_independence.statement: The positive ordinates gamma_1, gamma_2, ... are Q-linearly independent.
gamma_n_linear_or_algebraic_independence.named_conjecture: Linear Independence Conjecture (LI, Wintner 1935; Ingham 1942; Rubinstein-Sarnak 1994)

dirichlet_L_functions.summary: Nontrivial zeros of Dirichlet L(s, chi) in 0 < Re(s) < 1 have the same open irrationality/transcendence status as zeta(s) (even the nonvanishing L(1/2, chi) != 0 at the single algebraic point s = 1/2 is Chowla's conjecture, still open in general).

dedekind_and_automorphic_L_functions.summary: For Dedekind zeta_K(s) and GL(N) automorphic L-functions (Lagarias 2004, arXiv:math/0404394v4), global zero sums (Li coefficients) are expressed via logarithmic derivatives of completed L-functions, while individual critical-strip zero locations have open arithmetic status.

selberg_zeta_functions.summary: Selberg zeta zeros correspond to Laplace eigenvalues lambda_j = 1/4 + r_j^2 on hyperbolic surfaces; transcendence of individual non-explicit spectral parameters r_j is open.

exponential_polynomials.summary: For finite exponential polynomials sum_{j=1}^m a_j exp(omega_j s) with algebraic parameters, Lindemann-Weierstrass / Gelfond-Schneider / Baker control simple 2-term or commensurable zeros, whereas zeta(s) is an infinite Dirichlet series whose analytic continuation into 0 < Re(s) < 1 is NOT a finite exponential polynomial.

siegel_E_and_G_functions.summary: By the Siegel-Shidlovsky theorem (1929/1959) and Beukers (2006), if an E-function f(z) in Q_bar[[z]] satisfies a linear differential equation over Q_bar(z), its values and non-singular zeros are transcendental. OBSTRUCTION FOR ZETA: By Hilbert (1900) and Ostrowski (1920), zeta(s) is differentially transcendental (satisfies NO algebraic differential equation), and its Dirichlet series sum n^{-s} is a power series in p^{-s}, not an E-function in s.

arxiv_primary_sources_used.title: Zeta functions over zeros of general zeta and L-functions
Zeta functions over zeros of Zeta functions and an exponential-asymptotic view of the Riemann Hypothesis
Arithmetic of linear forms involving odd zeta values
A note on odd zeta values
Many odd zeta values are irrational
A note on the irrationality of zeta_2(5)
On the irrationality of certain p-adic zeta values
A Note on a Recent Attempt to Prove the Irrationality of zeta(5)

transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: Distinct algebraic numbers alpha_1, ..., alpha_m in Q_bar such that exp(alpha_j) satisfy a nontrivial Q_bar-linear relation.
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: If rho in Q_bar, the terms n^{-rho} = exp(-rho log n) have exponents -rho log n which are transcendental for all n >= 2 (since log n notin Q_bar), and the critical-strip analytic continuation is an infinite non-absolutely-convergent limit, not a finite Q_bar-linear relation among exp(alpha_j) for alpha_j in Q_bar.

transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: Algebraic base alpha in Q_bar \ {0, 1} and irrational algebraic exponent beta in Q_bar \ Q such that alpha^beta lies in Q_bar.
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: Assuming rho in Q_bar \ Q makes each individual prime power p^{-rho} transcendental by Gelfond-Schneider, but zeta(rho) = 0 is a vanishing analytic continuation of an infinite sum/product, which does NOT force any single p^{-rho} or pi^{-rho/2} to be algebraic.

transcendence_theorem_applicability.theorem: Baker's theorem on linear forms in logarithms (1966)
transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: A finite linear combination beta_0 + beta_1 log(alpha_1) + ... + beta_m log(alpha_m) with alpha_j, beta_j in Q_bar.
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: zeta(rho) = 0 is a relation among infinitely many exponentials n^{-rho} (via analytic continuation), not a finite linear form in logarithms of algebraic numbers; furthermore, the Euler product log zeta(s) = -sum_p log(1 - p^{-s}) diverges in 0 < Re(s) < 1.

transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: A vector of E-functions f_1(z), ..., f_m(z) in Q_bar[[z]] satisfying a first-order system of linear differential equations over Q_bar(z), evaluated at a non-singular alpha in Q_bar^x.
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: zeta(s) is NOT an E-function in s, and by Ostrowski (1920) / Hilbert (1900) zeta(s) satisfies NO algebraic differential equation over C(s) whatsoever.

transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: Meromorphic functions f_1, ..., f_d of finite order with transcendence degree >= 2 such that d/ds maps the ring K[f_1, ..., f_d] into itself (algebraic differential ring), simultaneously taking values in a number field K at sufficiently many points.
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: Neither zeta(s) nor Gamma(s/2) generates a finitely generated ring closed under d/ds (both are differentially transcendental), and a single hypothetical algebraic zero rho gives only one evaluation point where zeta(rho) = 0 while zeta'(rho), zeta''(rho), ... have unknown arithmetic nature.

transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: Values of Ramanujan quasi-modular Eisenstein series E_2(q), E_4(q), E_6(q) at an algebraic modular parameter q in (0, 1) (yielding algebraic independence of pi, e^pi, Gamma(1/4)).
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: Nesterenko's theorem controls special modular periods at CM / algebraic nomina q (which correspond to Gamma(1/4), Gamma(1/3), pi, e^pi), NOT the Mellin integral of theta_3(it) at an off-lattice complex exponent rho in 0 < Re(rho) < 1.

In xi(rho) = 0, the factor pi^{-rho/2} is multiplied by (1/2)rho(rho-1)Gamma(rho/2)zeta(rho); because zeta(rho) = 0 makes the entire product vanish (0 = 0), no algebraic value is assigned to pi^{-rho/2}.

transcendence_theorem_applicability.theorem: Transcendence of Gamma(alpha) at algebraic alpha (Chudnovsky 1976; Rohrlich-Lang)
transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: Evaluation of Gamma(alpha) at special rational points alpha in {1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6} (where Gamma(alpha) is transcendental via CM elliptic periods).
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: 1) For general algebraic alpha in Q_bar \ Q (and even most rationals p/q), transcendence of Gamma(alpha) is itself OPEN; 2) At a nontrivial zero rho, Gamma(rho/2) has no zeros or poles and is multiplied by zeta(rho) = 0, yielding no equation constraining Gamma(rho/2).

transcendence_theorem_applicability.theorem: Differential transcendence of Gamma (Holder 1887) and zeta (Hilbert 1900 / Ostrowski 1920)
transcendence_theorem_applicability.input_structure_required: An identically satisfied polynomial differential relation P(s, f(s), f'(s), ..., f^{(n)}(s)) = 0 for all s in an open domain.
transcendence_theorem_applicability.obstruction: Differential transcendence is a functional identity statement over C(s); a differentially transcendental function can have arbitrary prescribed algebraic or rational zeros (e.g., (s - alpha) * Gamma(s) is differentially transcendental and vanishes at s = alpha).

zero_order_identity.explanation: Because zeta(rho) = 0 and the archimedean prefactor A(s) = (1/2)s(s-1)pi^{-s/2}Gamma(s/2) is nonzero everywhere on 0 < Re(s) < 1, zeta(1 - rho) = 0 follows, while dividing xi(rho) = xi(1 - rho) by zeta(rho) = 0 is division by zero and strictly invalid.

first_derivative_at_simple_zero.expanded_identity: A(rho) * zeta'(rho) = -A(1 - rho) * zeta'(1 - rho)  (since zeta(rho) = zeta(1 - rho) = 0)
first_derivative_at_simple_zero.ratio_identity: zeta'(rho) / zeta'(1 - rho) = -A(1 - rho) / A(rho) = -pi^{rho - 1/2} * Gamma((1 - rho)/2) / Gamma(rho/2) = -chi(1 - rho)
first_derivative_at_simple_zero.why_no_contradiction_arises: Even if rho in Q_bar is assumed, the derivative values zeta'(rho) and zeta'(1 - rho) have completely unknown arithmetic nature (they are NOT constrained to be algebraic), and the transcendence status of pi^{rho - 1/2} * Gamma((1 - rho)/2) / Gamma(rho/2) at a non-real algebraic point rho = beta + i*gamma (gamma != 0) is also unknown.

euler_product_firewall.fallacy_blocked: The argument 'each Euler factor (1 - p^{-rho})^{-1} is nonzero, therefore zeta(rho) != 0' is invalid in 0 < Re(s) < 1 because the infinite Euler product diverges there and analytic continuation does not preserve nonvanishing of divergent infinite products.

xi_hadamard_product_status.canonical_weierstrass_product: xi(s) = xi(0) * exp(b_0 * s) * prod_rho (1 - s/rho) exp(s/rho), where b_0 = xi'(0)/xi(0) = log(2*sqrt(pi)) - 1 - gamma_E/2 = -S_1
xi_hadamard_product_status.symmetric_paired_product: xi(s) = xi(0) * lim_{T -> infty} prod_{|Im(rho)| <= T} (1 - s/rho) = xi(0) * prod_{{rho, 1-rho}} (1 - s(1 - s) / (rho(1 - rho)))
xi_hadamard_product_status.why_exponential_factors_cancel_under_sym: Pairing rho with 1 - rho (or conj(rho) on the critical line) gives 1/rho + 1/(1 - rho) = 1/(rho(1 - rho)) = O(|gamma_rho|^{-2}). Since sum_rho |gamma_rho|^{-2} < infty by Riemann-von Mangoldt N(T) = O(T log T), the Weierstrass convergence factors exp(s(1/rho + 1/(1 - rho))) have convergent exponent sum S_1 * s, which cancels exp(b_0 * s) = exp(-S_1 * s) identically.
xi_hadamard_product_status.unpaired_product_warning: Writing xi(s) = xi(0) prod_rho (1 - s/rho) WITHOUT specifying symmetric pairing |Im(rho)| <= T or (rho, 1 - rho) grouping is invalid because sum_rho |rho|^{-1} = infty.
primary_citations: Titchmarsh (1986), The Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function, Section 2.12

reciprocal_sum_S1.ordering_convention: lim_{T -> infty} sum_{|Im(rho)| <= T} (1 / rho) = (1/2) sum_rho (1/rho + 1/(1 - rho))
reciprocal_sum_S1.exact_formula: 1 + gamma_E / 2 - log(2 * sqrt(pi)) = 1 + gamma_E / 2 - log(2) - (1/2) * log(pi)
derivation_steps: 1. Write xi(s) = (1 - s) * pi^{-s/2} * Gamma(1 + s/2) * (-zeta(s)) near s = 0.
2. Differentiate log xi(s) at s = 0 using zeta(0) = -1/2, zeta'(0) = -(1/2)log(2*pi), and (d/ds)log Gamma(1 + s/2)|_{s=0} = (1/2)psi(1) = -gamma_E/2.
3. Obtain xi'(0)/xi(0) = -1 - (1/2)log(pi) - gamma_E/2 + log(2*pi) = log(2*sqrt(pi)) - 1 - gamma_E/2.
4. From the symmetrically paired Hadamard product xi(s) = xi(0) prod^{sym}(1 - s/rho), xi'(0)/xi(0) = -sum_rho^{sym} (1/rho), giving S_1 = -xi'(0)/xi(0) = 1 + gamma_E/2 - log(2*sqrt(pi)).

reflection_invariant_sum.why_absolutely_convergent: |rho(1 - rho)| = |1/4 - z_rho^2| ~ gamma_rho^2 as |gamma_rho| -> infty, and sum_rho gamma_rho^{-2} < infty because N(T) = O(T log T).

reciprocal_sum_S2.equivalence_identity_between_s0_and_s1: 2 * zeta''(0) + log(2 * pi)^2 = gamma_E^2 - pi^2 / 12 + 2 * gamma_1
constants_entering: First Stieltjes constant gamma_1 (or equivalently zeta''(0) and log(2*pi))

reciprocal_power_hierarchy.absolute_convergence_for_m_ge_2: For every integer m >= 2, sum_rho |rho|^{-m} < infty by partial summation against N(T) = (T/(2*pi))log(T/(2*pi)) - T/(2*pi) + O(log T) = O(T log T), since int_2^infty T^{-m} log T dT < infty for m >= 2.

odd_centered_sums_vanish.proof: Under functional-equation reflection rho <-> 1 - rho, z_{1-rho} = -z_rho, so z_rho^{-(2m-1)} + (-z_rho)^{-(2m-1)} = 0 identically; equivalently, log Xi(z) is an even analytic function at z = 0.

even_centered_sums.simpler_than_uncentered_note: Unlike S_m at s = 0/1 where log(-zeta(s)) has an explicit Laurent expansion in gamma_E and Stieltjes constants gamma_k, centered sums Sigma_{2m} at s = 1/2 depend onzeta^{(k)}(1/2)/zeta(1/2), which have no simpler closed form in classic constants; however, all odd centered sums vanish identically by reflection symmetry.

quartet_polynomial.global_symmetric_relation: The global centered invariant Sigma_2 = sum_rho z_rho^{-2} determines the sum over quartets of -c2 / c0 = 4*(delta^2 - gamma^2)/(delta^2 + gamma^2)^2, and Sigma_4 determines the sum of (c2^2 - 2*c0)/c0^2, but global symmetric sums cannot isolate an individual quartet's (delta_rho, gamma_rho).

li_coefficient_audit.li_criterion: lambda_n > 0 for all n >= 1  <=>  RH (Li 1997; Bombieri-Lagarias 1999)
primary_citations: E. Bombieri and J. C. Lagarias (1999), J. Number Theory 77, 274-287

families_studied_by_voros.uncentered_superzeta: Z_zeros(s) = sum_rho rho^{-s} (and Hurwitz shift sum_rho (rho + v)^{-s})
families_studied_by_voros.centered_quadratic_superzeta: Z(sigma, x) = sum_{k>=1} (tau_k^2 + x^2)^{-sigma} where rho_k = 1/2 +- i*tau_k

analytic_continuation_status.summary: Voros (2003, Ann. Inst. Fourier 53, 665-699, arXiv:math/0104051v4; 2005, arXiv:math/0311029v1; 2010 Springer monograph; 2014, arXiv:1403.4558v2) proved meromorphic continuation of both superzeta families to all s in C via explicit-formula contour integral representations involving log xi(s) and the incomplete Gamma / Gram-Jorgenson-Lang expansion.

special_values_and_regularized_products.negative_odd_values_of_quadratic_superze: Expressible explicitly in terms of Bernoulli numbers, pi, log(2*pi), and derivatives of log Gamma
special_values_and_regularized_products.zeta_regularized_determinant: exp(-d/ds|_{s=0} sum_rho (rho - s_0)^{-s}) recovers the Hadamard product xi(s_0)/xi(0) up to explicit elementary/Archimedean anomaly factors (Voros 2003, Theorem 1).

arithmetic_nature_of_positive_special_va.explanation: Although Z_zeros(m) = S_m has an exact closed form in terms of gamma_E, pi, log(2*pi), zeta(2k+1), and Stieltjes constants gamma_j, NO positive integer value S_m (m >= 1) has proved rationality, irrationality, or transcendence in the literature because the irrationality and algebraic independence of gamma_E and Stieltjes constants gamma_j are open.

primary_citations: A. Voros (2005), in Number Theory, Physics and Geometry (arXiv:math/0311029v1)
A. Voros (2010), Zeta Functions over Zeros of Zeta Functions, Springer LNUMI Vol. 8

main_unresolved_constants: gamma_E (Euler's constant: even irrationality is open)
log(pi) (irrationality/transcendence of log(pi) and Q-linear independence of {1, gamma_E, log(4*pi)} are open)
Possible rational cancellation between gamma_E and log(4*pi) is unexcluded

gamma_E, gamma_1, gamma_2, gamma_3 (Stieltjes constants vs. pi^4)
psi_1(1/4) = pi^2 + 8*G (Catalan's constant G, irrationality open)
gamma_E, log(4*pi), pi^{2k}, zeta(2k+1), Stieltjes constants gamma_0, ..., gamma_{n-1}

apery_1979_zeta3.theorem: zeta(3) notin Q (irrationality exponent mu(zeta(3)) < 5.5138800, Giraudin 2026 arXiv:2609.26980v1; Rhin-Viola 2001).
apery_1979_zeta3.citation: R. Apery (1979), Asterisque 61, 11-13; F. Beukers (1979), Bull. London Math. Soc. 11, 268-272.

rivoal_2000_ball_rivoal_2001_infinite_od.theorem: dim_Q span_Q(1, zeta(3), zeta(5), ..., zeta(2n+1)) >= ((1 + o(1))/(1 + log 2)) log n; in particular, infinitely many odd zeta values are irrational.
rivoal_2000_ball_rivoal_2001_infinite_od.citation: T. Rivoal (2000), C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 331, 267-270; K. Ball and T. Rivoal (2001), Invent. Math. 146, 193-207.

zudilin_2001_one_of_four.theorem: At least one of the four odd zeta values {zeta(5), zeta(7), zeta(9), zeta(11)} is irrational.
zudilin_2001_one_of_four.citation: W. Zudilin (2001), Russ. Math. Surveys 56(4), 149-150; Izv. Math. 66 (2002), 489-542 (arXiv:math/0104249v1; arXiv:math/0206176v2).

rivoal_zudilin_2018_two_among_69.theorem: At least two of the odd zeta values {zeta(5), zeta(7), ..., zeta(69)} are irrational.
rivoal_zudilin_2018_two_among_69.citation: T. Rivoal and W. Zudilin (2018/2020), Compos. Math. 156 (arXiv:1803.03160v1).

fischler_sprang_zudilin_2019_subexponent.theorem: At least 2^{(1 - eps) log s / log log s} odd zeta values between 3 and s are irrational.
fischler_sprang_zudilin_2019_subexponent.citation: S. Fischler, J. Sprang, and W. Zudilin (2019), Compos. Math. 155(5), 938-952 (arXiv:1803.08905v2).

lai_sprang_zudilin_2025_2adic_zeta2_5.theorem: The 2-adic Kubota-Leopoldt zeta value zeta_2(5) is irrational (following Calegari-Dimitrov-Tang on zeta_2(3) and Lai-Lupu-Sprang 2025 arXiv:2505.23088v1 on p-adic Zudilin tuples).
lai_sprang_zudilin_2025_2adic_zeta2_5.citation: L. Lai, J. Sprang, and W. Zudilin (May 2025), 'A note on the irrationality of zeta_2(5)', arXiv:2505.05005v2.

refuted_2024_preprint_on_archimedean_zet.claim_inspected: S. Suman (July 2024), 'A note on the Irrationality of zeta(5) and Higher Odd Zeta Values', arXiv:2407.07121 [math.GM].
refuted_2024_preprint_on_archimedean_zet.refutation: Explicitly refuted by K. Chen, W. He, Y. He, Y. Huang, Y. Li, Q. Tang, L. Wu, S. Xu, S. Yang, and Z. Yu (Nov 2024), 'A Note on a Recent Attempt to Prove the Irrationality of zeta(5)', arXiv:2411.16774v3.

zeta5_current_status.record_correction: Individual irrationality of the Archimedean constant zeta(5) remains OPEN_IN_LITERATURE (explicitly restated as open in Lai-Lupu-Sprang May 2025, arXiv:2505.23088v1). The verified recent 2025 breakthrough by Lai-Sprang-Zudilin (arXiv:2505.05005v2) proves the irrationality of the 2-adic zeta value zeta_2(5), while the 2024 math.GM claim for Archimedean zeta(5) (arXiv:2407.07121) was refuted in arXiv:2411.16774v3.

structural_comparison_table.zeta_m_arithmetic: Yes: fixed positive integer m in Z_{>=2} (known rational/integer input).
structural_comparison_table.zeta_rho_eq_0_arithmetic: No: rho = beta + i*gamma in {0 < Re(s) < 1} is the unknown target.

structural_comparison_table.zeta_m_arithmetic: No: zeta(m) in R is the unknown target whose irrationality is tested.
structural_comparison_table.zeta_rho_eq_0_arithmetic: Yes: zeta(rho) = 0 is fixed identically to zero.

structural_comparison_table.zeta_m_arithmetic: Yes: Beukers/MZV hypercube integrals int_{[0,1]^m} ... and Ball-Rivoal well-poised hypergeometric series sum_{k>=1} R_n(k) with integer poles of fixed multiplicity m.
structural_comparison_table.zeta_rho_eq_0_arithmetic: No: m enters as the integer dimension of the hypercube [0,1]^m or the integer pole order of (k + j)^{-m} in partial-fraction decomposition; neither exists for complex non-integer rho.

structural_comparison_table.zeta_m_arithmetic: Linear form L_n = A_n * zeta(m) + B_n (or sum_{j} A_{n,j} zeta(2j+1) + B_n) with A_n, B_n in Q and common denominator d_n^m.
structural_comparison_table.zeta_rho_eq_0_arithmetic: Setting m -> rho in A_n * zeta(rho) + B_n gives A_n * 0 + B_n = B_n, which eliminates zeta(rho) completely and leaves no small nonzero linear form in rho.

structural_comparison_table.zeta_m_arithmetic: Yes: integer shifts k + 1, ..., k + n in Q allow lcm(1..n)^m denominator control.
structural_comparison_table.zeta_rho_eq_0_arithmetic: Only under a reductio assumption rho in Q_bar, where rho appears in exponents k^{-rho}.

structural_comparison_table.zeta_m_arithmetic: Rational function R_n(t) with integer poles whose residues produce rational combinations of zeta(j).
structural_comparison_table.zeta_rho_eq_0_arithmetic: Would require P_n(X) in Z[X] with 0 < |P_n(rho)| < C^{-n}, which zeta(rho) = 0 does not generate.

method_by_method_transfer_test.method: Apery (1979) / Beukers (1979) hypercube integral I_n = int_{[0,1]^m} P_n(x_1).../(1 - x_1...x_m) dx
method_by_method_transfer_test.object_produced_for_zeta_m: I_n = A_n * zeta(m) - B_n with d_n^m I_n in Z and 0 < |I_n| -> 0 (for m = 2, 3).
method_by_method_transfer_test.what_fails_when_m_replaced_by_rho: 1) The integral dimension m must be a positive integer; 2) Even in fractional Mellin form, evaluating at zeta(rho) = 0 makes A_n * zeta(rho) - B_n = -B_n != 0 of order O(1) instead of exponentially small O(r^n).

method_by_method_transfer_test.method: Ball-Rivoal (2001) / Zudilin (2001) / Fischler-Sprang-Zudilin (2019) hypergeometric series sum_{k>=1} R_n(k)

required_ingredients_for_auxiliary_polyn: 1. A sequence of nonzero integer polynomials P_n(X) in Z[X] \ {0} of degree d_n <= D_n and height H(P_n) <= e^{h_n}.
2. Nonvanishing certificate: P_n(alpha) != 0 for the target alpha in {rho_1, gamma_1} for infinitely many n.
3. Analytic upper bound: |P_n(alpha)| <= exp(-U_n) derived from an analytic identity (such as Cauchy/Jensen on an entire function with high-order zeros).

4. Liouville / Mahler algebraic lower bound: If alpha in Q_bar of degree d and Mahler measure M(alpha), then P_n(alpha) != 0 implies |P_n(alpha)| >= (d_n + 1)^{-(d-1)} H(P_n)^{-d + 1} M(alpha)^{-d_n d}.
5. Asymptotic contradiction inequality: U_n > (d - 1) h_n + d * log M(alpha) * d_n for large n.

why_zeta_rho_eq_0_does_not_supply_P_n.for_P_n_of_rho_1: Taylor polynomials T_N(s) of xi(s) (or zeta(s)) have transcendental coefficients (involving log(pi), gamma_E, Stieltjes constants gamma_k, and zeta^{(k)}(0)), NOT integer/algebraic coefficients; conversely, Dirichlet partial sums sum_{m=1}^N m^{-s} are polynomials in p^{-s} = exp(-s log p), not polynomials in s, and do not converge exponentially to 0 at s = rho_1 inside 0 < Re(s) < 1.
why_zeta_rho_eq_0_does_not_supply_P_n.for_P_n_of_gamma_1: Replacing rho_1 by gamma_1 via Xi(i*gamma_1) = xi(1/2 + i*gamma_1) = 0 produces an even power series sum_{m>=0} c_{2m} gamma_1^{2m} = 0 whose coefficients c_{2m} = (-1)^m Xi^{(2m)}(0)/(2m)! are themselves transcendental/unknown constants (related to Sigma_{2m}), so truncating it does not yield P_n(gamma_1) in Z[gamma_1].

gamma_function_firewall.general_rational_values_status: For general rational p/q notin {1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6} mod Z (e.g., Gamma(1/5)), individual transcendence of Gamma(p/q) is OPEN (Rohrlich-Lang conjecture; Wolfart-Wustholz 1985 give linear-independence bounds on beta values).
gamma_function_firewall.general_complex_algebraic_values_status: For non-real algebraic alpha = (beta + i*gamma)/2 in Q_bar \ R, NO general theorem establishes transcendence or algebraic independence of Gamma(alpha).
gamma_function_firewall.obstruction_for_functional_equation: In xi(rho) = (1/2)rho(rho-1)pi^{-rho/2}Gamma(rho/2)zeta(rho), neither Gamma(rho/2) nor pi^{-rho/2}Gamma(rho/2) has known arithmetic properties at a hypothetical non-real algebraic rho, blocking any naive functional-equation transcendence contradiction.

differential_transcendence_firewall.holder_theorem_gamma: Holder (1887): Gamma(s) satisfies no algebraic differential equation over C(s).
differential_transcendence_firewall.hilbert_ostrowski_theorem_zeta: Hilbert (1900) / Ostrowski (1920): zeta(s) satisfies no algebraic differential equation over C(s).
differential_transcendence_firewall.counterexample_to_zero_inference: For any prescribed algebraic number alpha in Q_bar, the entire function F_alpha(s) = (s - alpha) / Gamma(s) (or (s - alpha) * xi(s)) is differentially transcendental over C(s), yet vanishes at the algebraic point s = alpha. Hence differential transcendence of a function never implies transcendence of its zeros.
